### Sutra-sthana: Chapter 19 (143)

A clever physician should remove the discharge by gently stroking or massaging the wounds caused by <term>kapha</term> <gloss>phlegm</gloss> and <term>vayu</term> <gloss>wind/air</gloss> multiple times to clear the impurities. 39. The wound should be pressed from below, following the direction of the hair growth to drain the fluids. All deep-seated joints and connections should be properly aligned. 40. In joining the lips, one should follow the methods previously described. A physician who understands the joints should use their intelligence to apply the appropriate bandages for broken bones as prescribed. 41.

Whether rising, sitting, going to bed, walking, or traveling in various vehicles, the wound of such a person <note>who has been properly bandaged</note> will not suffer further injury or pain. 42. Wounds located in the joints, bones, or abdominal cavities; those affecting the <term>shira</term> <gloss>veins/channels</gloss> and <term>snayu</term> <gloss>tendons/ligaments</gloss>; as well as deep-seated, serious, and irregularly shaped wounds cannot be successfully treated without proper bandaging. 43.

Thus ends the eighteenth chapter in the Sutra-sthana of the Sushruta Samhita. 18.

<note>This concludes the Hindi commentary by Pandit Muralidhar Sharma on the eighteenth chapter.</note>

### Nineteenth Chapter: 19

Now we shall explain the chapter titled the Nursing and Care of the Wounded <term>Vranitopasaniya</term>.

From here begins the exposition of the chapter on the rules of conduct and environment for patients with wounds.

First, one should seek a suitable house for the wounded patient. This house should be built on auspicious land and have a favorable layout. 1. In a house built on auspicious ground, kept clean, free from scorching sunlight, and protected from strong winds, the patient will not suffer from bodily, external, or mental diseases. 2. In that house, one should provide a bed that is spacious, well-covered with soft bedding, pleasing to the mind, and positioned with the head toward the East. Weapons should also be kept nearby. 3. On a well-spread bed, the wounded patient can move comfortably. The head is bowed toward the East because the gods reside in that direction, and this position honors them. 4.

<summary>This page concludes the instructions on surgical bandaging and begins the nineteenth chapter regarding the proper environment and nursing care for wounded patients, emphasizing auspicious placement and hygiene.</summary>
